quotes.excerpt: Land of Never #1 is a nice start to a very promising series. The initial premise will grab your attention, but the teased tie in will make you sit up in your seat. The artwork is fantastic and leaves nothing to the imagination as it captures the story completely. This is a must grab at the shop this week. Give this first issue a shot and consider adding it to your Pull List, or at the very least order the second issue to see where it goes.

Land of Never takes a familiar tale and twists it into something truly unsettling. Steve Orlando delivers a gripping mystery fueled by a desperate father, all while Miguel Mora illustrates atmospheric tension that jumps from the page. Land of Never is the version of an age-old classic that you never knew you needed, a blend of heart and horror. Cannot wait for what is coming next.

Conan The Barbarian #33 sets sail when Conan and the Red Brotherhood are shipwrecked on a mysterious island after encountering a massive storm and a supernatural attacker. Jim Zub’s start to the latest arc is as strong as ever, and Fernando Dagnino’s artwork is a perfect fit. 10 out of 10. No notes.

This was a solid issue that carries a real sense of danger and presents readers with a problem that only someone like James T. Kirk could likely solve. There is also a great observation made by both Kirk and Jurati about Sato, which has been a recurring theme throughout the series so far. Sato is a captain who is often held back from making the tough choices because of his own fears and self-doubt.
Gonzalez delivers stunning art throughout the issue. I absolutely love the character designs and the attention to detail in every page and panel.

The Uncanny X-Men #32 brings this out-of-this-world arc to an end and we’re left on a very interesting note of uncertainty, sadness, and love. Gail Simone makes you feel every emotion and leaves you wanting more.

When the Nur try wiping out the Brood, they forgot what party they crashed! Simone’s writing balances the heartfelt drama with outright fun themes. The art centers in on the chaotic scene with great success. This has been such a refreshing change of pace story that reminds fans to push the creative boundaries on the stat quo X-tales.

The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is an amazing opening issue for the series that will surely trap readers’ interest in reading more of the series. The mysteries that this issue either straight out tells us or implies are enough to peek even the most jaded readers’ interest. The premise that is laid out here in the first issue is intriguing, but when you know that Panosian obviously has more in store for us that jacks the intrigued levels all the way up. This should be a slam dunk pick up at the shop or Neon Ichiban this week. As a matter of fact, make sure to add this one to your Pull List as you won’t want to miss a single issue of this series.
The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is a solid debut issue. It takes a familiar concept and puts it in a setting that feels rather new and fresh.

Sonic the Hedgehog x Godzilla #1 is exactly what you want from a crossover like this. It moves with energy, delivers big spectacle, and understands the appeal of both worlds without overcomplicating things. Nick Marino keeps the story light on its feet while letting the concept do the heavy lifting, and the art team turns every page into a showcase of motion and destruction. It may skew toward a younger audience, but the craft and pacing make it easy for anyone to get swept up in the ride. If this issue is any indication, this is a crossover built to entertain first and ask questions later.

Sonic the Hedgehog X Godzilla is that crossover that sounds odd on paper, yet someone capture the best of both franchises in a one wild package. Writer Nick Marino and artist Jack Lawrence deliver a fun, campy adventure while still giving Godzilla and the kaiju roster that presence we expect. Sonic the Hedgehog X Godzilla is a fun crossover that proves the Blue Blur and the King of the Monsters are a great match.
Transformers #34 brings explosive action, sharp world-building, and major character moments as Optimus, Cliffjumper, and Thundercracker face new threats and shifting alliances.

Transformers #34 does a good job of setting up where we are going with the Bots left on Earth. The different threads of the story look like they will be the roots of what will happen over the next issues. This issue is a little slower than what we’ve become accustomed to, but that’s not a bad thing as it does a great job of laying groundwork for the future. Transformers continues to be one of the best and most consistent titles on the shelf every month and should definitely not be overlooked.
Power Rangers: Green #1 delivers a unique take on the post-apocalyptic story, and a new version of Tommy Oliver.

This debut issue brings back an iconic original Ranger in a futuristic setting. No longer a practicing Ranger, but the last Ranger in existence. Teaming up with an old foe to take on a new threat that is bringing Tommy out of retirement. This issue doesn’t answer some of the more pivotal questions surrounding Tommy, but it paints a comforting picture that he is living a more simplistic life. This is a must-read for Power Ranger fans! So make sure you pick up your copy of this new miniseries and add this to your “pull list.”A little bonus for this review! I had the opportunity to speak with Pallie Paul Allor about this issue as well as what readers can expect in issue two. If you are a fan of Alpha, you are going to want to see what he does in this debut issue because it leads to much more from him physically in issue two!
G.I. Joe #25 is a major milestone done right, paying off years of buildup and kicking off the series' most epic storyline yet.

G.I. JOE #25 is a phenomenal start to the Nightforce story arc. Joshua Williamson, Tom Reilly and Andrea Milana pace things out that you feel like you are experiencing the start of a big blockbuster event. Everything that happens in this issue comes across as being a payoff for many sub-plots that have been developed since the start of the series. Where the payoff leads to is anyone’s guess, leaving you as the reader even more excited to find out what happens next.

Superman #40 wraps up one big event, leads us into another, and hints at the future for Superboy Prime. With Clark Kent set to return soon, Prime won’t be front and center, but I think he’s shown that he can be a more than average substitute for the Man of Steel.
Williamson, Mora and Sanchez roll the dice in walking a fine line of genius and insanity with CK’s heroic methods. Another display of high level storytelling for a very polarizing character.

FINAL GRADE: 9.8The Suns ride again into the belly of the beast with a non-stop thrilling adventure. MacKay steers events into a surprise twist ending, but the art steals the show on this one. Pramanik & Rosenberg present a magnificent display of combat & drama. You won’t be ready for what unfolds here!

It’s all hands on deck as ‘Marc Spector: Moon Knight’ #6 brings back a classic Marvel team to help the moonlit vigilante save his family. Marvel canon is woven perfectly into a modern tale as the visuals turn the dial all the way to eleven once more.

The Smart Division is a fantastic science-fiction mystery that eerily could be more fact than fiction. Writer Zack Kaplan delivers a timely detective tale exploring the use of modern technology in solving crimes. However, it’s the juxtaposition of John Pearson’s elegant brush strokes that makes story rise above the rest. Kaplan and Pearson’s creativity knows no bounds and The Smart Division is proof of that.

I sat down with The Smart Division expecting a slick sci-fi detective story and walked away rattled about the world outside my window. That is the highest thing I can say about a comic right now. This is a perfect debut and one of the most relevant books on the stands, and I cannot wait to see where the case goes.

Operation: Iron Coffin comes out of the gate swinging with a unique premise that delivers far more than ever expected. Kenny Porter and Tyrell Cannon give us a Dracula that isn’t just here for the carnage, although we get plenty of that, but for a compelling redemption arc wrapped in a fast-paced, blood-soaked WWII setting. IDW Dark may have some heavy hitting titles in its first year as an imprint at IDW Publishing, but Operation: Iron Coffin stands out as one of the best.

Operation Coffin #1 is a stylish debut for Porter and Cannon’s new take on Dracula. A truly unique premise, backed by engaging lore and a curious mission have already laid the groundwork for a wild ride ahead.

While this series has just four issues and that might not seem like a lot of space to tell such an intense tale, The Horror of Godzilla #1 has already set things up for horrific greatness. You’re never going to look at the King of the Monsters the same way again.

The Horror of Godzilla #1 is exactly what the title promises, an incredibly terrifying look at the King of the Monsters through the eyes of those caught in their path. Writers Ethan S. Parker and Griffin Sheridan deliver on of the most unsettling Godzilla stories I have ever experienced, while Tristan Jones brings his A-game with artwork that is both impactful and horrifying. The Horror of Godzilla is one of the most frightening Godzilla stories with some of the best illustrations I have seen in recent memory, making it a strong contender for comic of the year.

A tragic past reveal sparks an explosive search for present day answers as Batman is on the hunt! Taylor pens a striking tale of loss and heart in this latest chapter. Janín exposes the a hero’s last moments with stunning art. This series never falters on delivering high marks.
Detective Comics #1111 ramps up the action and mystery in the latest issue, while also showcasing the great potential of having Batman team up with additional heroes.

The Uncanny X-Men #32 brings this out-of-this-world arc to an end and we’re left on a very interesting note of uncertainty, sadness, and love. Gail Simone makes you feel every emotion and leaves you wanting more.

When the Nur try wiping out the Brood, they forgot what party they crashed! Simone’s writing balances the heartfelt drama with outright fun themes. The art centers in on the chaotic scene with great success. This has been such a refreshing change of pace story that reminds fans to push the creative boundaries on the stat quo X-tales.

An origin story centered around one of the main book’s killers could have easily gone sideways, but thankfully that’s simply not the case with Rascal Randy. Instead, fans have an up-close look at several compelling characters and insight into one of the most unpredictable and twisted characters in comics.

If you finished Exquisite Corpses Season 1 wanting more from Rascal Randy, this new series is exactly what you had hope for. Tyler Boss expands on the history of the character without taking away some of the mystery in the main series. Boss delivers a creepy, atmospheric story that stands confidently on its own while adding to the lore Exquisite Corpses. Exquisite Corpses: Rascal Randy is one of those rare prequels that doesn’t just justify its existence, it makes an already iconic character even more fascinating.

The Flash #35 is another winning chapter that reminds readers why Wally West remains one of DC's most endearing heroes. Ryan North balances inventive superhero concepts with genuine heart, while Gavin Guidry's artwork radiates personality from start to finish. The central idea of preventing disasters before they happen opens up exciting possibilities, and the creative team wisely leaves enough uncertainty to keep you wondering where it all leads. Even before the larger questions arrive, this issue succeeds by making heroism feel joyful, hopeful, and endlessly fun.

Wally West’s obsession with the future leads to more hijinks as events speed along. North leans heavily into the scientific portion of plans with the writing. Guidry and Lucas craft solid looks at this new scheme via the art. An interesting take leading into more fast problems down the road. Don’t miss out.

I’m sure some of the rhetoric in this issue, particularly out of Mia’s mouth, will get a lot of people talking about certain real-world parallels, but this comic actually works really well justin the context of a superhero story. This is a world where the innocent are hunted and the guilty are more powerful than ever, and the heroes are often powerless to strike back – so villain tactics might be necessary to fight back.

Absolute Green Arrow #2 takes us deeper into the mystery of who our killer is. This issue brings us to familiar faces within the Green Arrow lore and shrouds us in mystery even more than before. The blend of action and suspense is working cleverly, making this a horror story of sorts. I will have this run at the very top of my pull pile every month; I hope it gets expanded beyond its current limited run.

Given the overall arc of things, it's actually kind of difficult to tell exactly where things are going to end up by the end of the series. Theoretically, there could be some sort of a triumphant thing going on here. And certainly developments that occur at the end of the issue seemed to suggest there might be something far more interesting beyond the edge of the final panel. But it's going to be a pretty bleak journey through the remaining shadows of the central plot arc.

If Destruction Be Our Lot #4 is a dark, emotional chapter that pushes Abe to his lowest point while also giving the series a stronger sense of mystery and momentum. The issue handles addiction, isolation, and disbelief with real weight, making Abe’s search for the truth feel personal and urgent. With strong writing, bleak but effective artwork, and an ending that opens the door to something bigger, this continues to be a smart, thought provoking series that is absolutely worth following.

Batman and company embarks on a plan for justice and closure in this excellent arc finale! Taylor’s writing reveals many hidden gems while bringing down the house. Janín brings out the inner turmoil of guilt, speeding into strong finishing pages. Time and time again, Detective Comics delivers on everything you want from a Batman comic!
Detective Comics #1112 wraps up the current Prion mystery in extremely satisfying ways that also highlight the true power of the lead character: his humanity.

Zod’s victorious ways are upended by a twist you won’t see coming in a magnificent crossover chapter. Williamson reshuffles the deck with a strong script. The art team gives the action a bold look with sensational sequences. Buckle in for where this story heads from here!
Superman #41 delivers one of the most brutal battles between the Man of Steel and General Zod as the "Kingdom of Zod" hits its halfway point.

Lets see if Grønbekk picks up the seeds planted in this storyline after the Bad Seeds event. Black Mask is still out there. And we never got an ending for Holly. Just Falcone saying she was “safe”. There is still a lot of meat on the bone here.

Kyle Rayner sees a ghost from his past as his new hometown city cooks up more mischief along the way. Adams balances the heavier drama with more fun moments. The art teams bring out the emotional scars with a side of laughs in the art. You’ve never seen Los Angeles looking this emerald green!

Rom makes his presence known early in a solid showcase issue. Kirkman welcomes the Space Knight into the EU with a great script. Hughes and Delpeche capture some mystery behind the noble actions with strong art. Get ready for another excellent addition to comics’ most unpredictable universe!

Void Rivals #33 introduces ROM the Space Knight to the Sacred Ring castaways with loads of heart, charm, and action. Kirkman’s choice to bring in ROM is a master stroke, and the art team’s construction of an alien world is excellent.

Poison Ivy #47 is an exciting climax of a long-ongoing descent into chaos that the book has been building up to across several issues. As a prelude, the issue perfectly sets up Batman: Bad Seeds, and gives readers a taste of the mayhem that they can expect from the crossover event. If the rest of the crossover is as good as this prelude, we are in for a wild and intense ride.

Mayor Isley’s frantic attempt to maintain power pushes the city to its’ breaking point. Wilson shows the pressure finally breaking Isley to an extreme level. Fernandez & Prianto show how fast politics can break a soul. Seeds are planted for what’s coming next and readers won’t want to miss it!

Spawn #378 slows things down to establish the players circling Al Simmons while reinforcing just how dangerous the world has become. Much of the issue will feel familiar to longtime readers, particularly the recap of Al's past, but the vampire meeting and mysterious butcher keep the larger story intriguing. Stephen Segovia makes the most of the limited action, delivering a ferocious finish that reminds us exactly what Spawn can do.
X-Men #36 is packed full of philosophical debates and action-packed artwork, as DNX continues to loom on the horizon.

A great issue that sets up for the DNX event in a really compelling way. It sets things off in a way that feels like it’s already too late to stop it and it’s going to be interesting to see where it leads from here. Jed MacKay’s great story, together with the artwork that’s absolutely incredible make this an issue you can’t pass up on!

A question of checks and balances lead the JLU into troubling times as Despero strikes. Waid presents a compelling argument behind great action sequences. The art team shines when unlocking a colossal confrontation. No one ever said Amnesty came without a cost.
Justice League Unlimited #22 delivers both hard-hitting action and heightens the stakes as distrust between team members threatens to tear the group apart and have far-reaching consequences.

Harley Quinn #65 delivers a fun and explosive conclusion to Harley’s split-personality storyline, while finally giving the series a stronger sense of direction. The recent issues have successfully rebuilt momentum, adding new emotional depth to Harley and setting up her role in Batman: Bad Seeds. Not every idea lands perfectly, but this is an entertaining payoff that leaves Harley in an exciting place for what comes next.
The Flash #36 continues Ryan North and Gavin Guidry's stellar run on the title, delivering a perfect entry point for new readers while adding to the ongoing story of Wally's new power set.

Wally West takes his bold gamble to Metropolis but another hero is not on board with his actions. North takes a traditional approach to superhero team-ups with the script. Guidry and Lucas showcase the more light-hearted aspects of a friendly pairing with solid art. With every action, there is a great reaction. What that will be for this story remains to be seen.

reason.snippet: ‘Zatanna’ #5 brings Zatanna back to The Hidden City of the Homo Magi where she has to confront her feelings over losing her mother while trying to save the city.
pros: Zatanna's personality and emotions were able to shine a bit more during this issue
Jamal Campbell and Andrew Dalhouse were able to create a truly terrifying scene of the flame spirit
Zatanna's grief manifesting in anger was beautifully written and isn't something we see often.
cons: I wish the flame spirit and its connection to the Hidden City was explored more in this issue rather than leaving it for the next issue.

pros: ROM ends up feeling exactly as he should
The artwork is fantastic and fluid with great design work on ROM's new look especially
There is a clear feeling of reverence and love for the source material while still trying to do something new
cons: It took a minute for ROM's characterization to settle in

Javier Garrón delivers excellent action and scale, while the bizarre collection of heroes and Knullified opponents makes nearly every matchup fun. The issue can get chaotic, but a genuinely surprising cliffhanger proves this series still has…
pros: Javier Garrón delivers huge, dynamic action throughout
Creative matchups make the extended battle entertaining
A legitimately surprising cliffhanger
cons: Mostly just a fight comic and not much else

reason.snippet: Amazing Spider-Man #35 (LGY #999) does exactly what a penultimate milestone issue needs to do, putting Peter Parker’s personal life under serious pressure while keeping the superhero action moving. Joe Kelly juggles Aunt May, Damage Control, Peter’s space friends, and Ghost-Spider without making the issue feel overcrowded, while Francesco Manna delivers strong action and some surprisingly emotiona…
pros: Strong balance between Peter Parker drama and superhero action
Aunt May storyline gives the issue real emotional weight
Kelly continues to make Symbie, Raelith, and Glitch endearing additions
cons: Ghost-Spider’s sudden turn is underdeveloped, though by design
Some readers may still find Peter’s space crew an unusual fit for Amazing Spider-Man

reason.snippet: Black Cat #13 shows that you can turn enemies into friends...or at the very least acquaintances. It also makes for a brief respite before the next issue tosses Felicia headfirst into the chaos of Queen in Black.
pros: Keeps up the mix of wit and action that's defined this title.
Wilson manages to tie two story arcs together in a surprising way, and adds more depth to the Punisher in the process.
Genolet brings a living nightmare to life in the form of the monster Frank and Felicia have to fight.
Reber's color art highlight the absurdity of witnessing a fight between two antiheroes and a Lovecraftian monster on the beach.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Batwoman #6 is an intriguing issue that explores Beth’s psychology a little bit deeper, and fills readers in on an unseen chapter in the character’s backstory. This retrospective accomplishes the task of providing the audience with an explanation for how and why Beth decided to take on her sister’s identity, even going as far as posing as Batwoman.
pros: Fascinating and deep exploration of Beth’s mental state as we see her coping with trauma by assuming her twin sister’s identity
Jeff Spokes’ art in this issue delivers a refreshing tonal shift by switching up the visual language of the book with a brighter and warmer color palette
cons: As this a flashback story, I do question how essential this issue is in the larger narrative, and whether readers could follow Beth’s character arc without havi…

reason.snippet: Solid action is undermined by the hollow execution of tropes readers will see coming. Bishop #3 delivers on the superhero fights, but not much else.
pros: The action, especially in the first half is really well done.
The rotation between Reese Hannigan and Mario Santoro is really well handled, making the book flow well and providing for some visual variety.
cons: The characterization and dialogue is extremely bland. The story doesn't give readers a reason to care about these characters.
The plot doesn't have much intrigue and the issue moves at about the speed a reader would expect.
